title: Cognitive and Behavioral Development of 9-Year-Old Children After Maternal Cancer During Pregnancy: A Prospective Multicenter Cohort Study.
ehr_evidence: The study uses a multicenter cohort study with neurocognitive test batteries and parent-report behavioral questionnaires; no mention of EHR or linked health data.
summary: A multicenter cohort study evaluating the long-term cognitive and behavioral outcomes of 9-year-old children prenatally exposed to maternal cancer and its treatments (chemotherapy, surgery, radiotherapy).
key_findings: Mean cognitive and behavioral outcomes were within normal ranges.
No significant differences in FSIQ based on treatment type, cancer stage, or sex.
Positive association between gestational age and FSIQ.
Maternal bereavement before age 2 was associated with lower FSIQ when adjusted for GA.
Maternal education level was a significant predictor of FSIQ.
study_design: Prospective multicenter cohort study (cross-sectional analysis of 9-year-olds)
population: 151 children (mean age 9.3 years) from Belgium, Netherlands, Italy, Czech Republic, and New Jersey
exposure_domain: maternal cancer and treatment during pregnancy
limitations: Small sample size for specific subgroups
Potential confounding from maternal stress or insecure attachment
Lack of general population comparison for remedial support rates
data_availability_statement: We report a cross-sectional analysis of the 9-year-old children (Data Supplement, online only).
